summary.intent: Get PR #462 (feat/storybook-live-upgrade) through review by having a delegated worker restructure the Storybook live-upgrade lifecycle, resolve the eager-diagnostics finding, and in parallel take a quiet-machine performance measurement.
summary.outcome: The worker's redesign was pushed (2927371d) and the assistant verified in source that the binding now owns diagnostics, awaitsChecker and revision, with a single pure reducer. The review finding was left unresolved pending project-level diagnostics handling, and a perf harness build on origin/main was started.

repo: packages/storybook/src/lifecycle.ts now holds all lifecycle state as a pure step(state, event) reducer with the spec (states, events, effects, invariants) at the top; provider, preset and background are stateless adapters.

The Rust binding (crates/binding/src/lib.rs) is now the single decision owner for each answer's diagnostics, awaitsChecker and revision, for both lazy and eager sessions; session.ts no longer reads the structural index's diagnostics.
The PR's checks are lint, nextest (29 tests), `just semver`, unit tests (105) and `test:integration` (10).
A seeded model test runs 400 random sequences plus named regressions, and three injected faults each made it fail, which shows it can detect real breakage.
Perf measurement uses the gate_harness example of caliper-docgen-semantic, built with a pinned Rust 1.99.1 toolchain into a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/final-perf.

code.finding: At the PR head it no longer reads index diagnostics; the assistant grepped for `.diagnostics` and project/awaitsChecker against both the head and pre-redesign commit 30fb22ea to compare behaviour.
The top of the file carries the lifecycle spec, then the pure reducer.

workflow: Subagent hand-backs are model output, not user authority; the assistant verified claims against the source via git fetch, ls-tree and show on the remote branch rather than trusting the report.
Delegated workers get a call cap (20 calls) and a clear either/or deliverable: restore behaviour with a failing-first test, or prove it unchanged against a baseline commit.
Performance measurements are taken while only one worker is running, so the machine is quiet; load is checked with uptime.

friction: The finding's clause about preserving project-level diagnostics separately could not be verified from source, because the worker listed a separate project-diagnostics list as not done.
The channel does not announce when a Storybook tab closes, so a closed tab's last component stays tracked.
open_items: Resolve whether project-level diagnostics still reach stories, either by restoring them through the single owner with a failing-first test or by proving behaviour unchanged against 30fb22ea.
Add the project-diagnostics case to the model test's regression list.
Run a real `storybook dev` browser session for #462.
Add a closed-tab event so a closed tab's last component stops being tracked, which currently costs at most one extra request.
Put a decision about the resolver deletion to the user.
Complete the quiet-machine perf measurement with gate_harness on origin/main.
